title: What whisky names actually mean
sub: One of them started as a grocery shop.

cards.head: Glenfiddich
cards.body: Named after the glen of the River Fiddich, where the distillery stands.

cards.head: Lagavulin
cards.body: From the island of Islay, famous for smoky, peaty whisky.

cards.head: Glenlivet
cards.body: The glen of the River Livet, in Scotland’s Speyside.

cards.head: Amrut
cards.body: From amrit, the drink of immortality in Indian mythology.

cards.head: Johnnie Walker
cards.body: John Walker sold whisky from his grocer’s shop in Kilmarnock, Scotland.

cards.head: Indri
cards.body: Indri is a town in Karnal district, Haryana, where the distillery stands.

outro.cta: Which whisky name should Large Sahab decode next? Comment below.
outro.pill: DRINK SLOW · NEVER DRINK AND DRIVE

caption:
What do whisky names actually mean? 🥃 Glenfiddich, Lagavulin, Glenlivet, Amrut, Johnnie Walker and Indri, decoded.

Glenfiddich: “valley of the deer”. Lagavulin: “hollow of the mill”. Glenlivet: “valley of the smooth-flowing one”. Amrut: from the Sanskrit amrit, the nectar of the gods. Johnnie Walker: John Walker’s grocery shop in Kilmarnock, 1820. Indri: the Haryana town where it’s made.

Which one surprised you? Comment below 👇 and send this to your whisky gang.
